issues.reason: Pinning the undergoer to Theme is licensed by the instruction set's own role doctrine -- a direct object is Patient only when the action creates / destroys / consumes / physically changes it, and 'when the test is unclear, default to Theme' -- and the 'likeliest answer' premise fails anyway, since the context's burn event carries wintergloss (Patient) and mire_essence (Alongside), not the moths.

(Inheritance nightmoth moth) is the mandatory genus of a transparently modifier+head solid compound (Compound concepts: 'always emit the genus'; 'the solid spelling is never a reason to skip decomposition'), so any compliant parse that mentions nightmoths puts that atom in the KB and the conjunct does not narrow the match against a compliant KB.

gaps_confirmed: 'What happens to X?' has no prescribed query shape -- the instruction set gives only the agentive open-verb counterpart ('What does Bob do?' -> (Member $e $verb) (Agent $e $b)), the Patient-vs-Theme test cannot be applied with the verb left unknown, and role storage is not among the closed dual-storage-union instances, so no union over undergoer roles is licensed either.
new_gaps: A locative PP in a 'what happens to X at L?' question has two coherent attachment sites -- a standing position on the entity, (LocatedIn $g <place>), or the locus of the happening, (Location $e <place>) -- and the instruction set decides neither while requiring a question to be translated single-form (Multiple live readings: 'a question about this sentence is still translated per Queries, single-form'); a licensed form would need either an attachment rule for questions or a union over the two storages.
notes: Referent handling is right: 'that lantern' resolves straight to the context constant sk_lantern_1 per Input, and 'at' -> LocatedIn is the licensed entity-attached containment head. What remains is role and attachment underspecification -- gap territory over a query whose every conjunct is true and well-typed.
